name: LLM Privacy Challenge
description: The NeurIPS 2024 LLM Privacy Challenge addresses privacy risks in Large Language Models (LLMs) by focusing on identifying vulnerabilities (Red Team) and developing defenses (Blue Team) using synthetic datasets mimicking private data.

cr:input.name: Synthetic Private Data
cr:input.description: Synthetic datasets generated to mimic real-world private information, such as replacing names and email addresses in public datasets like Enron with randomly generated strings. The data format is designed to simulate sensitive data contexts responsibly.
cr:input.contentUrl: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset download URL]

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: Expected outputs include attack success rates (Red Team) and defense effectiveness metrics (Blue Team). For example, Red Team outputs might include extracted sensitive information, while Blue Team outputs could include sanitized LLM responses.

field.name: attack_accuracy
field.description: The success rate of identifying and extracting sensitive information from LLMs. Example values: 0.85 (85% success rate).

field.name: efficiency
field.description: For Red Team: number of tokens or queries used to achieve a successful breach. For Blue Team: computational overhead of defense mechanisms. Example values: 120 tokens for Red Team, 0.02 seconds per query for Blue Team.

field.name: model_effectiveness
field.description: For Blue Team: general performance of the LLM after applying defensive methods. Example values: 0.92 (92% accuracy on benchmark tasks).

cr:evaluation.notes: Attack accuracy is maximized for Red Team and minimized for Blue Team. Efficiency measures resource use (e.g., tokens, computational overhead). Model effectiveness evaluates LLM performance post-defense.
